{{nihongo|'''Ikagu Shrine'''|伊香具神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Kinoshimo Town, Oto, {{ill|Nagahama, Shiga|Q844130|qid=Q844130}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was classified as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}. Its shrine crest is the “Upper Wisteria.” {{nihongo|'''Ikagu Shrine'''|伊香具神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

It is称ed one of the most prominent shrines in the Kohoku region. The {{ill|Okonai|Q11291908|qid=Q11291908}} ritual is held on February 24.

Its torii gate is of a unique style known as the Ikagu-style torii, the only one of its kind in Japan. It is said to resemble a combination of the great torii of {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|Q191763|qid=Q191763}} and the triple torii of {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|Q705542|qid=Q705542}}.

== Enshrined Deity ==
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ikatsumi-no-Mikoto}}
This deity is said to be identical with “Ikato-mi,” who appears in the hagoromo (feather robe) legend found in fragments of the {{ill|Ōmi no Kuni Fudoki|Q11638480|qid=Q11638480}}, and is believed to possess divine virtues that bring abundant harvests.

== History ==
In ancient times, when the area was still an undeveloped marshland, the enshrined deity is said to have come and reclaimed the land, later enshrining himself here to protect his descendants (according to the {{ill|Ōmi Yochi Shiryaku|Q85883966|qid=Q85883966}}). It is also said that before the 10th year of the Hakuhō era during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}}, a descendant named Ikano Sukune Toyoatsu built the shrine buildings (according to the “Shrine Origin Record”<ref>Nishikawa, cited in “Ikagu Shrine.”</ref>).

In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} era ({{ill|859|ab|859|af|859|am|859 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|859|ar|859|ary|859|arz|859|ast|859|avk|859|az|859|azb|۸۵۹ (میلادی)|bar|859|bcl|859|be|859|be_x_old|859|bg|859|bn|৮৫৯|bpy|মারি ৮৫৯|br|859|bs|859.|ca|859|cdo|859 nièng|ceb|859|ckb|٨٥٩|crh|859|cs|859|csb|859|cv|859|cy|859|da|859|de|859|el|859|eml|859|eo|859|es|859|et|859|eu|859|fa|۸۵۹ (میلادی)|fi|859|fo|859|fr|859|fy|859|ga|859|gan|859年|gd|859|gl|859|he|859|hi|859|hr|859.|ht|859 (almanak jilyen)|hu|859|hy|859|id|859|ilo|859|io|859|is|859|it|859|ja|859年|jv|859|ka|859|kaa|859|kk|859 жыл|ko|859년|la|859|lb|859|lij|859|lmo|859|lt|859 m.|lv|859. gads|map_bms|859|mdf|859|mg|859|mhr|859|mk|859|mr|इ.स. ८५९|mrj|859 и|ms|859|mzn|۸۵۹|nah|859|nap|859|nds|859|new|सन् ८५९|nl|859|nn|859|no|859|nrm|859|nso|859|oc|859|or|୮୫୯|os|859-æм аз|pl|859|pnb|859|pt|859|qu|859|ro|859|ru|859 год|rue|859|sa|८५९|scn|859|sd|859ع|se|859|sh|859.|shn|859|si|859|sk|859|sl|859|smn|859|sq|859|sr|859|su|859|sv|859|sw|859|tg|Соли 859|th|พ.ศ. 1402|tk|859|tl|859|tly|859|tr|859|tt|859 ел|uk|859|ur|859ء|uz|859|vec|859|vi|859|vls|859|war|859|wuu|859年|xmf|859|zh|859年|zh_min_nan|859 nî|zh_yue|859年|qid=Q23897}}), the shrine was promoted from Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade, Merit Rank Eight to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade<ref>Entry of the 27th day of the first month of the same year in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}.</ref>, and in the 8th year it was further promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade<ref>Entry of the intercalary 3rd month, 7th day of the same year in the Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku.</ref>. Under the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engi system}}, it was listed as a Myōjin Taisha. According to shrine tradition, in the 7th year of {{ill|Kanpyō (era)|Q1346292|qid=Q1346292}} ({{ill|895|Q31119|qid=Q31119}}), {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}} personally copied the {{ill|Lotus Sutra|Q861212|qid=Q861212}} and the {{ill|Golden Light Sutra|Q391694|qid=Q391694}} and dedicated them to the shrine, at which time an imperial plaque bearing the title “Shōichi-i Kun Itto Taisha Daimyōjin Kongōkaku-in Bosatsu” was bestowed<ref name="西川">Nishikawa, “Ikagu Shrine.”</ref>.

Later, {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|Q297107|qid=Q297107}} donated 200 {{ill|Koku|Q855048|qid=Q855048|lt=koku}} of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine land}} and requested that prayers be conducted on the 18th day of the first, fifth, and ninth months. The {{ill|Azai clan|Q1872031|qid=Q1872031}} also extended its patronage. However, during the warfare of the {{ill|Battle of Shizugatake|Q225562|qid=Q225562}}, the shrine buildings and ancient records were destroyed by fire, and the shrine lands were confiscated<ref name="西川"/>.

In the 8th year of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} ({{ill|1875|Q7764|qid=Q7764}}), it was designated a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, promoted to Prefectural Shrine in the 32nd year, and in the 40th year designated a shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and silk from the government.
